course_description:
They left the water, conquered the land, and took to the skies. They can be friends: providing invaluable pollination and nutrient recycling ecosystem services, but they can be foes: pest species can sometimes reach plague proportions. Some are masters of disguise, while others flaunt their spectacular beauty. Insects are undoubtedly the most successful animal group, in diversity, geography and ecology. They are also a rich part of our environment, economy and culture. This is a course for the budding entomologist and will train you in professional entomological skills: (1) insect identification, (2) specimen preparation, (3) advanced microscopy, and (4) communication.

Majority of the student cohort in BIOL2205 are science students who have declared the Minor in Entomology , but you'll learn with other students from agricultural science, ecology, environmental science, environmental management, biomedical science, biotechnology and wildlife science who are taking the course as elective study.ﾠ

Additional timetable information
BIOL2205 Insect Science expects students to attend weekly 4-hour practicals. These have been designed for you to develop entomological skills that are highly relevant to entomology careers: including specimen preparation, scanning electron microscopy, field sampling techniques and more. Most practicals are laboratory-based, but there are two practicals where you will undertake on-campus fieldwork (field sampling to learn about the varied ways of sampling for arthropods) and two practicals when you will attend excursions to meet professional entomologists at Queensland Museum and Biosecurity Queensland (no additional costs required).
course_aims: To enable students to recognise the major groups of insects and appreciate the role these insects play in the ecosystem.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand the significance of insects in environmental, economic, and social contexts
Characterise (identify) an insect specimen to the Order and Sub-Order taxonomic level
Prepare insect specimens for the purposes of insect identification to a professional standard
Read and appraise entomological literature critically

assessment_details.title: Insect collection
assessment_details.task_description: Collecting insects provides valuable insight into their habitat, distribution, biology and behaviour and makes their identification easier and more meaningful. You will assemble an insect collection (presented using professional standards) that evidence your ability to classify diverse insects (to Order level). You will complete this task individually, and should complete your own collection and identification. This includes humanely killing insects. You may purchase your own pinning board, box, and supplies if you intend to keep your own insect collection, or you may borrow equipment from us (loan), but these must be returned to us by the end of the course. learning_activities.topic: No practical No practical Learning outcomes: L01

Practical 1 (Laboratory) Receive insect collection kit; contents and collection assignment explained; pinning techniques demonstrated; displays of example collections and common pinning mistakes; practice insects provided for students to learn proper pinning and labelling techniques. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Practical 2 (Laboratory) Practice using dichotomous keys and identify insect orders; view examples of various orders; use of AI Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Excursion 1 Visit to Queensland Museum entomological and zoological curation department. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Practical 3 (Laboratory) Continuing examples of insect orders and practise identification; explanation of scanning electron microscopy assignment; SEM techniques; project planning, specimen selection and preparation; time slot sign-up Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Scanning Electron Microscopy Week Attend registered timeslot to use SEM and photograph specimens for assessment. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04

Practical 4 (Fieldwork) Walk around campus looking for insects; collecting methods demonstrated: sweep netting, beat sheeting; trapping methods explained: set up pitfall traps, Malaise traps, flight intercept traps. Any hand collected insects can be brought back to the lab for identification. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Practical 5 (Fieldwork) Walk around campus looking for insects; collecting methods as before (sweep netting, beat sheeting); traps set up in previous weeks are cleared. Insects can be brought back to the lab for identification. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Practical 6 (Laboratory) Open invitation for you to bring in up to five specimens from your insect collection (which should be in progress by this time) to get feedback on quality and composition of your specimen preparation and pinning technique.
Excursion 2 Visit to Biosecurity Queensland (top secret!!!) Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Practical Exam The practical exam will take place in this week during the usual timetabled practical timeslot. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Practical 7 (Fieldwork) There will not be a practical session in the day during the usual timetabled session. Instead, you are invited to attend a night catch that will take place at the UQ Lakes Natural Amphitheatre to observe and collect nocturnal insects. We will include pizzas for everyone who attends! Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Practical 8 (Laboratory) Learning consolidation and final touches on your insect collection before submission. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
